nodes.label: Phase 3 â€” React Three Fiber Migration Plan
nodes.norm_label: phase 3 a€” react three fiber migration plan

nodes.label: GameController (imperative three.js)
nodes.rationale: ~1000 lines of imperative three.js construction tightly bound to a single requestAnimationFrame loop driving both rendering and cannon physics. Identified as the primary migration target because component reuse is hard, hot-reload is impossible, testing is painful, and onboarding is slow.

nodes.label: React Three Fiber (R3F)
nodes.rationale: Chosen over imperative three.js for declarative scene description, Suspense for asset loading, and a community ecosystem (@react-three/cannon, @react-three/drei, @react-three/postprocessing).

nodes.label: src/r3f/sceneDSL.js â€” Scene DSL
nodes.rationale: Declarative scene-description format that builds vanilla three.js objects today and maps 1:1 onto R3F JSX. Enables bottle/block/particle entities to be expressed as ~30 lines of data instead of ~150 lines of imperative ceremony, making entities testable and R3F-ready without requiring the full stack upgrade.

nodes.label: CameraController (State Machine Rewrite)
nodes.rationale: Complete rewrite of CameraController.js as a state machine driven by user spec: front-facing label always centered, shoulder pitch, random projection swap, three random mid-flip modes, failed-state grading. Label tracking uses block-travel axis (not bottle label normal) to avoid clipping into restaurant walls, with bottle inner-mesh yaw forcibly overridden each frame via setLabelFaceDirection.

nodes.label: Label Tracking Design â€” Block-Travel Axis Strategy
nodes.rationale: Camera position uses the block-travel axis (currentâ†’next block, ground-projected) not the bottle's actual label normal. This guarantees a clean sightline along the gameplay path without ever clipping into props. Bottle inner-mesh yaw is forcibly rotated each frame so the label always faces the camera; override suspended during FLIP state so the bottle can spin freely mid-air.
nodes.norm_label: label tracking design a€” block-travel axis strategy

nodes.label: Three Flip Camera Modes (FOLLOW/LOCKED/CINEMATIC_CUT)
nodes.rationale: Random mid-flip behaviour selected by injected RNG: FOLLOW tracks bottle in flight, LOCKED snapshots pose allowing off-frame travel, CINEMATIC_CUT hard-cuts to perpendicular side-on pose. RNG-injectable for deterministic test coverage.

nodes.label: Random Projection Swap (Ortho/Persp) on Landing
nodes.rationale: Each LANDING transition coin-flips between OrthographicCamera and PerspectiveCamera. Pose is carried over to the new active camera so the swap is invisible until the next breathing/lerp tick. Both cameras share fade overlay (each parented to one) so failed-state grading works regardless of active projection.

nodes.label: Cannon Physics Integration
nodes.rationale: Identified as highest-risk R3F migration item. Currently hand-rolled world.step()+body sync; target is @react-three/cannon <Physics>. Tween+physics+game-state machine are tightly interleaved; deterministic event log in gameStore + replay test are the mitigation strategy.

nodes.label: @tweenjs/tween.js
nodes.rationale: Unmaintained. R3F community uses framer-motion-3d or motion-three. Migration of every tween call site is a separate week of work that can happen in parallel with sub-phase 3c.

nodes.label: _computeTargetZoom â€” View-Space Extent Fitting
nodes.rationale: Projects bottle and landing-zone positions into camera view space via dot product with camera local X/Y axes, adds CAM_ZOOM_PADDING (1.5 world units), then takes the smaller zoom of both axes (more zoomed out) so both fit, clamped to [CAM_ZOOM_MIN, CAM_ZOOM_MAX]. Avoids per-frame allocation by reusing _camRight, _camUp, _zoomOffset vectors.

nodes.label: UI Group Counter-Scale Compensation
nodes.rationale: UI group is counter-positioned and counter-scaled (scale = 1/camera.zoom, position = camera frustum edge / zoom) so score text maintains screen-corner position and world size regardless of zoom level.

nodes.label: Dual Zoom Damping (flip vs idle)
nodes.rationale: During flips (500ms) uses _flipDamping=14 (same as camera position damping) so zoom reaches target before bottle reaches arc peak. During idle block-to-block transitions uses gentler _zoomDamping=3 for cinematic feel. Two damping values serve different perceptual goals.

nodes.label: Ground Plane 3x Enlargement for Zoom-Out
nodes.rationale: At CAM_ZOOM_MIN=0.55 the visible area grows to 1/0.55â‰ˆ1.82x the frustum. The original 1.2x ground multiplier would leave void at edges. Enlarged to 3x to cover any zoom level with margin.

nodes.label: Element-wise Projection Matrix Lerp
nodes.rationale: Both OrthographicCamera and PerspectiveCamera stay alive in scene graph. Per-frame, the host camera's projectionMatrix is overridden with an element-wise lerp of the two cameras' native matrices. At blend=0 host gets ortho matrix; at blend=1 host gets persp matrix; in between the user perceives a continuous dolly-zoom-like warp rather than a mode swap. Chosen over instant swap because the prior approach only matched bottle size at swap time, leaving foreshortening as a single-frame snap.

nodes.label: Projection Blend State (_targetProjectionBlend / _smoothedProjectionBlend)
nodes.rationale: _targetProjectionBlend flips instantly when setProjection is called; _smoothedProjectionBlend lerps toward it each frame with PROJECTION_BLEND_DAMPING=1.6 (~95% in 1.9s). activeCamera is selected by smoothed blend â‰¥0.5, making the host swap a visual no-op (both cameras render the same blended matrix at the crossover frame).

nodes.label: PROJECTION_BLEND_DAMPING = 1.6
nodes.rationale: 1.6 gives ~95% convergence in 1.9s â€” sweet spot where user no longer perceives two camera modes but also doesn't notice transition starting/ending. Above ~3 reintroduces brutal-feeling snap; below ~1.0 transition drags so long the next flip can interrupt mid-blend.

nodes.label: Regression Test â€” No Perceptual Snap (15% frame-delta bound)
nodes.rationale: Asserts that no single update() call changes any projection matrix element by more than 15% of the total endpoint delta. A hard cut would be 100% on one frame; the lerp distributes it over ~30 frames, keeping the per-frame ratio well under 15%.
nodes.norm_label: regression test a€” no perceptual snap (15% frame-delta bound)
